SYR.text:
The old regime fell in December 2024, and the headlines moved on. The hunger did not. The UN counted 15.6 million people in Syria who need humanitarian help in 2026, about 6 in 10 people there.

Families are going home. More than 1.3 million Syrians came back from abroad in the year after the fall, often to destroyed homes, with a drought that aid groups described as the worst in 36 years.

The aid plan wants $2.92 billion and aims to reach 8.6 million people. Between January and July, help reached about 2.5 million people a month. Since mid May, aid groups also report money problems after a rule forced them to pay in Syrian pounds.

sources.name: UK Home Office country note, June 2026

SSD.text:
Two out of every three people in South Sudan need humanitarian help this year. The UN counts 10 million, up from 9.3 million a year ago, after new fighting, floods, disease outbreaks and people arriving from the war in Sudan. More than 1.3 million have crossed that border.

About 7.5 million people could face acute hunger in 2026, and at least 28,000 are already in the worst category, catastrophe. Hunger monitors warn of a risk of famine in parts of Jonglei and Upper Nile, where fighting blocks aid.

The aid plan asks for $1.46 billion, but it only aims at 4.3 million people, down from 5.4 million, because aid groups expect low funding. The UN says that choice left more than 2.4 million people in critical need without help last year.

sources.name: OCHA Humanitarian Action, South Sudan plan

COD.text:
Nearly 15 million people in the Democratic Republic of the Congo need humanitarian help, out of about 113 million. More than 5 million of them have been driven from their homes, mostly by fighting in the east.

The UN's count looks lower than last year's 21.2 million, but the UN says that comes from a new way of counting, not from things getting better. The 2026 plan asks for $1.4 billion and aims at 7.3 million people, because funding is short.

Last year the response got less than a quarter of the $2.5 billion it asked for. In the first three months of 2026, help reached about 3.6 million people, nearly 38 percent of the target.

BFA.text:
In Burkina Faso, 4.5 million people need help this year, and about 2 million have been forced from their homes. Armed groups have blockaded dozens of towns, and people inside report severe hunger.

In July, The New Humanitarian reported that civilians and aid workers accuse the army of stopping people from leaving some of those towns. It is unclear how many people are inside, but millions may be trapped. Some food arrives by airdrop and by military convoy.

The aid plan asks for $658.5 million and aims at 2.7 million people. By the UN's March figures only a small share of that money had arrived, so the response is thin where it is needed most.

NER.text:
About 3 million people in Niger need humanitarian help in 2026, in a country of more than 27 million. Armed groups keep pushing families out of their villages, mostly in Tillabéri, Diffa and Tahoua.

The numbers are moving the wrong way. The UN's food agency counted more than 161,000 people newly displaced so far this year, against 33,000 in the same stretch of 2025. By July, more than 548,000 people were displaced inside the country, about 20 percent more than a year before.

The aid plan asks for about $674 million. Last year it was only 26 percent funded, and the food agency says it needs new money just to keep helping the newly displaced.

sources.name: WFP country brief via ReliefWeb, March 2026

TCD.text:
Chad is a poor country that took in a huge number of people from a war next door. More than 900,000 Sudanese refugees have crossed into eastern Chad since April 2023, and in the eastern provinces about 1 in 3 people is now a refugee. 55,000 more arrived this year by late September.

Chad's own people need help too. The 2026 plan counts 4.5 million, around 40 percent of the country, and asks for nearly $1 billion.

In April, UN agencies warned of life-threatening cuts to food, water and shelter. Nearly 243,000 people were stranded in border areas because there was no money to move them to settlements further inland, and families slept in the open.

AFG.text:
Nearly half of Afghanistan needs humanitarian help this year: 21.9 million people, including more than 10.7 million women and girls. About 17.4 million face acute hunger, and 4.7 million of them are at emergency level.

Millions are also being sent home. About 2.6 million Afghans returned in 2025, mostly from Iran and Pakistan, and the UN expects around 2.7 million more in 2026. A separate $529 million plan was launched in May just to receive them.

The main aid plan asks for $1.71 billion to reach 17.5 million people. Aid groups warn that if the money falls short, hundreds of thousands could be left without shelter this winter.

PSE.text:
The UN counts 3.62 million people in need in the Occupied Palestinian Territory this year: 2.1 million in Gaza and 1.52 million in the West Bank. OCHA reported that 92 percent of housing units in Gaza had been destroyed as of October 2025, and that about 1.5 million people need emergency shelter supplies.

The 2026 appeal asks for $4.06 billion to reach 2.97 million people. By June it was less than 15 percent funded. By late August OCHA put it at 40 percent.

UNICEF reported in mid 2026 that more than 3,000 children a month were being admitted for malnutrition treatment in Gaza, well above pre-war levels. OCHA also warned in June that funding shortfalls were forcing partners to cut or suspend services.

SOM.text:
Somalia is slipping toward famine again. UN agencies warned of a confirmed famine risk in Burhakaba district, in the Bay region, where drought, high food prices and too little aid could push people into catastrophe if the rains fail. In February, 6.5 million people were in crisis level hunger or worse, 2 million of them in emergency.

The UN says 4.8 million people need help this year. That is 20 percent fewer than last year, but only because the rules for counting got stricter, not because life got easier. The plan asks for $852 million, 40 percent less than last year, and aims at 2.4 million people.

Even that smaller plan is mostly unfunded. Save the Children found it only about 15 percent funded in April 2026, the lowest level on record for that time of year, down from 28.8 percent funded in 2025.

YEM.text:
Half of Yemen needs humanitarian help this year: 22.3 million people, 2.8 million more than last year. About 70 percent of that need is in the north, which is run by the Houthi authorities.

That is where aid has been hit hardest. The UN says 73 of its staff are being arbitrarily detained by the Houthi authorities. In January the World Food Programme said it would end its operations in the north and terminate the contracts of all 365 of its staff there.

Money is running out as well. The 2025 plan was only about 28 percent funded, and in June the UN relief chief said this year's appeal was less than 15 percent funded. The plan aims to reach 12 million people.

UGA.text:
Uganda hosts more refugees than any other country in Africa: almost 2 million people, most of them from South Sudan and DR Congo. Anyone fleeing the fighting next door is let in and given land to farm. At the peak last year, about 460 people arrived every day.

The money has not kept pace. The 2026 refugee response plan needs about $850 million, and in September Uganda's parliament speaker said partners had provided only about 12 percent. UNHCR had received only 14 percent of its own $361 million by the end of March.

Aid groups say that means smaller food rations, thinner health care and more malnutrition in the settlements. WFP reported a shortfall of $47 million in March alone.

sources.name: UNHCR Uganda fact sheet, Jan to Mar 2026

MOZ.text:
In northern Mozambique, fighting in Cabo Delgado province has spread into new districts and into neighboring Nampula. UNHCR counts about 300,000 people newly displaced since April 2025. In February, IOM counted 661,532 displaced people across the country.

In July, aid agencies said at least 919,000 people in Cabo Delgado need help and only about half of them are getting it. The UN's conflict plan asks for $348 million to reach 1.1 million people in three northern provinces. About a third of it had been secured by July.

Mozambique has other emergencies on top of this. Floods and cyclones hit the central and south, so the whole 2026 plan asks for $534 million to reach 1.7 million people.

sources.name: UNHCR Mozambique update, Jan to Mar 2026

MLI.text:
In Mali, 5.1 million people need humanitarian help. Since September 2025, the armed group JNIM has tried to cut off fuel supplies to the south of the country, which pushed up prices and shut schools for weeks. On 25 April 2026, coordinated attacks on military targets escalated the fighting again.

One month into that escalation, the aid group IRC said families were struggling to find enough food, health care and water, and called Mali one of the world's most underreported crises. Aid workers recorded 814 access incidents in 2025, 41 percent more than the year before.

Money has been scarce. The 2025 plan was 26 percent funded, and by April only 16 percent of the 2026 appeal was covered. The UN's food agency later put it at about 22 percent.

HTI.text:
The UN Secretary-General called Haiti the most severe and fastest worsening humanitarian crisis in the Western hemisphere during a visit in June. 6.4 million people, more than half of all Haitians, need help, up from 5.5 million two years ago.

Gang violence has driven 1.4 million people from their homes, about 12 percent of the country. The number of displaced people doubled between September 2024 and October 2025, and food insecurity affects 5.7 million people, nearly 2 million of them at emergency level.

The 2026 plan asks for $880 million to help 4.2 million people. In June, the Secretary-General said barely a quarter of it was funded. Last year's appeal received only 24 percent.

MMR.text:
Nearly a third of Myanmar needs humanitarian help: 16.2 million people, about 5 million of them children. Armed conflict, disasters and a collapsing economy have displaced an estimated 3.6 million people, the highest figure on record. About half of them are in the northwest.

The 2025 earthquake, a 7.7 magnitude quake, hit a country already at war. Aid access has been severely restricted by fighting, red tape and threats to aid workers.

The 2026 plan asks for $890 million, 36 percent less than last year, and aims at only 4.9 million people, about 30 percent of those in need. In 2025 it received less money than in all of 2024.

CMR.text:
Cameroon has three crises at once. In the Far North, armed groups and climate shocks have driven out more than 500,000 people. In the North-West and South-West, a conflict that began in 2016 has displaced almost as many. In the east, more than 400,000 refugees from the Central African Republic are being hosted.

The UN counts 2.9 million people in need this year: 1.4 million in the Far North, 1.1 million in the North-West and South-West, and 337,000 among refugees. The plan asks for $308 million to reach 1.8 million people, which leaves about 1.1 million in need outside the plan.

By late August the plan was only about 26 percent funded. Cameroon is also one of eight pilot countries for the UN's "Global Humanitarian Reset", a plan to do more with less money.

HND.text:
Honduras lives with chronic violence, droughts and floods, and a steady stream of migrants and deportees passing through or sent back. In 2025 the UN counted 1.6 million people in need.

The money did not come. OCHA reports that the 2025 plan faced a 90 percent funding gap, with $14.4 million received of $138.5 million asked. As a result, aid groups cut their presence from 118 municipalities to just 33 for 2026. OCHA says this reflects less money, not less need.

Honduras then launched its own $75 million plan in March to help about 825,000 people in the places with the most unmet needs. Across Central America's Dry Corridor, the UN's food agency estimates 2.7 million people urgently need food help.

VEN.text:
About 7.9 million people in Venezuela, more than a quarter of the country, needed urgent humanitarian help at the start of 2026. The UN says the needs are in health, food, water, education and protection. Last year only 17 percent of the $600 million asked for was received.

Then the ground shook. In June, two earthquakes of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 struck the north-central part of the country. By mid July, the UN counted about 4,300 dead, 16,700 injured and 17,900 people with destroyed homes.

The UN added $299 million to the 2026 plan for 1.3 million quake survivors, bringing the total to $931 million. Before the quakes, the original plan was only 13 percent funded as of 20 April.

COL.text:
Colombia's war never fully ended, and it got worse in 2025. Armed groups now operate in 71 percent of its municipalities, according to UNICEF. The country has the highest level of conflict displacement in the Americas.

The sharpest edge is Catatumbo, near the Venezuelan border, where fighting between armed groups since January 2025 has forced people out and trapped others in their villages. The UN agency for refugees called it the country's most severe humanitarian crisis in a decade. By June 2026, aid agencies counted nearly 100,000 people displaced there.

The UN says 10.4 million people in Colombia need help in 2026, including migrants and refugees. In 2025, a 71 percent funding gap left 1.4 million people in need without help. Even after the plan was cut back, the gap was still 52 percent.

CAF.text:
In the Central African Republic, 2.3 million people, 35 percent of the population, need humanitarian help in 2026. As of the end of 2025, 427,479 people were displaced inside the country, and insecurity in the southeast has kept pushing families out.

The country is making progress toward stability, a senior OCHA official said in New York in May, but deep aid cuts now threaten the operation. The 2026 plan asks for $264.1 million to reach 1.3 million people.

Last year, in the first half alone, aid reached only 561,000 people, 32 percent of the target. The country's pooled humanitarian fund received just $13 million in 2025.

BGD.text:
More than 1.2 million Rohingya refugees live in crowded camps in Cox's Bazar and on Bhasan Char, many of them for nine years now. About 150,000 more have fled renewed violence in Myanmar since early 2024. They cannot move freely or work, so almost everything they eat depends on aid.

That aid is shrinking. This year's plan asks for $710.5 million, 26 percent less than last year and the lowest in a decade. In April, WFP started giving food aid only to those assessed as most in need, which affects 1.2 million refugees. A WFP assessment found that all Rohingya refugees were food insecure.

By late September the plan was about 50 percent funded. Last year donors met 46 percent of a $934.5 million appeal. In April 2026, a boat carrying Rohingya toward Malaysia sank after leaving Cox's Bazar, killing at least 250 people.

UKR.text:
Ukraine's war is in its fifth year, and the UN counts 10.8 million people who need humanitarian help in 2026. That includes people who fled their homes and people who stayed in towns close to the front line. IOM counted 3.5 million displaced people in August.

The biggest needs are near the front. The UN says 3.1 million people there need help, the highest level of need in the country. The 2026 plan asks for $2.3 billion to reach 4.1 million people.

In July, aid groups launched a winter plan asking for $358.4 million to reach 2.1 million people, focused on those closest to the front line and the newly displaced. Last year, the response reached 4.7 million people, 61 percent of its reduced target, while the appeal was 47 percent funded.

sources.name: UN Ukraine, Winter Response Plan, 22 Jul 2026
UNICEF Ukraine report, Jan to Sep 2026

VNM.text:
Vietnam is not a war zone, but 2025 gave it one of its worst typhoon seasons in decades. The UN says more than 4 million people were affected and damage reached $4.2 billion. Back to back storms, including Typhoons Bualoi and Matmo, brought floods and landslides to the north and the center.

The UN and the government drew up a joint response plan for 15 provinces. In May 2026, OCHA listed 1.4 million people in need, 0.7 million targeted and $61.1 million required.

By then only about $3 million, or 5 percent, had been received. Storms hit Vietnam every year, so these needs will come back.

sources.name: UN Vietnam joint response plan, Dec 2025

MDG.text:
Two cyclones hit Madagascar within ten days at the start of 2026. Fytia made landfall on 31 January and Gezani followed. More than 681,000 people were directly affected, and about 630,000 of them needed immediate help. The IFRC counted 62 deaths from Gezani alone and 14 from Fytia.

The cyclones landed on a country that was already in trouble. Years of drought in the south have cut harvests, and screening in 15 districts of the south and southeast found more than 4,500 children with severe acute malnutrition in the first three months of 2026.

The UN launched a $67.8 million flash appeal on 20 February to reach 486,012 people. WFP warned that broken supply lines had already forced it to suspend general food distributions for at least two months, and that it needed $37.6 million to resume.

sources.name: OCHA Madagascar snapshot, Jan to Mar 2026

LBN.text:
Before March, nearly 3 million people in Lebanon already needed humanitarian help. Then hostilities escalated on 2 March 2026, and by mid June OCHA counted about 1 million displaced people, 3,700 killed and 11,700 injured. UNICEF counted 253 children killed since 2 March, and 308,000 children displaced.

The UN launched a flash appeal on 13 March for $308.3 million and later raised it to $639.9 million to cover March to August, aiming at 1.4 million people. About 500,000 conflict-affected people had received multipurpose cash by April.

As of 29 June the appeal was 37 percent funded, with $237 million received.

sources.name: OCHA revised Flash Appeal, Mar to Aug 2026

CUB.text:
Cuba was hit twice. Hurricane Melissa struck the east as a Category 3 storm on 29 October 2025 and affected more than 2 million people, about one in five Cubans. Then, from January, imported fuel dwindled, and the energy crisis spread into water, health care, food and schools.

On 16 March, about 10 million people were left without electricity, according to OCHA. Daily power cuts have lasted 12 to 20 hours, and close to 1 million people depend on water trucks that often lack fuel. The UN has linked the fuel shortages to the end of supplies from Venezuela. OCHA has also pointed to a US executive order and other sanctions.

The UN revised its plan on 24 March to $94 million, aiming at 2 million of the 4.2 million people affected. By 1 May, only about a quarter of it was funded.

PAK.text:
Pakistan's 2025 monsoon was brutal. OCHA says the floods affected 6.9 million people, displaced 3 million and killed more than 1,000, including 275 children. Families in the mountainous north and in Punjab and Sindh are still rebuilding homes and livelihoods.

The UN's plan for relief and early recovery counts 2.8 million people in need and aims at 1.9 million. It asks for $64.9 million. In late January it had received $12.4 million, about 19 percent.

Pakistan also hosts around 3.7 million Afghan refugees, and many were caught in the floods. Between January and November 2025, Pakistan detained 102,249 Afghan nationals, according to UNICEF.

sources.name: UNICEF Pakistan report, Jan to Sep 2025

IRN.text:
War reached Iran in late February 2026. By April, UNHCR counted more than 3.2 million displaced across the country. OCHA reported more than 2,000 people killed, including more than 200 children, and more than 27,000 injured. WFP said 400,000 people in Tehran alone needed food help. By the end of July, more than 360,000 people were still displaced, while more than 820,000 had gone back to where they came from.

Iran also hosts about 1.65 million refugees, mostly Afghans. In February the UN launched an $80 million flash plan for March to May to help 2.8 million people, including refugees and host communities. By 11 May it was 47 percent funded.

The wider humanitarian appeal for Iran was far thinner. In April, aid agencies said it was funded at only 4.3 percent.

NGA.text:
The war in Nigeria's northeast has lasted 16 years. In Borno, Adamawa and Yobe, 5.9 million people need humanitarian help this year, and about 2.3 million have been displaced. WFP expects 15,000 people in Borno to face catastrophic, famine-like hunger.

Across the country, the UN's coordinator warned in Abuja that nearly 35 million Nigerians could face hunger in 2026. UNICEF counts 8.4 million people in need across the northeast, northwest and north-central regions, including 5 million children.

The plan asks for $516 million to reach 2.5 million people, down from 3.6 million last year. Because of limited funding, several treatment sites for malnourished children have closed in Borno, Adamawa and Yobe.

NPL.text:
On 26 August, a glacier collapse and landslide on Nepal's border with China sent a flash flood down the Bhotekoshi valley into Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading. The UN called it Nepal's deadliest natural disaster since the 2015 earthquake. About 84,270 people need humanitarian help, including more than 32,000 children, and some 4,500 displaced people were in holding centers in early September.

On 4 September the UN and its partners launched a $49.6 million flash appeal to reach more than 84,000 people over four months. The Red Cross movement launched its own appeal of 25 million Swiss francs.

By the end of September, the UN said the response had reached more than 64,000 people and was shifting toward recovery. UNICEF, for its part, reported that 43 percent of its own $17.2 million requirement was still unfunded on 22 September.

LKA.text:
Cyclone Ditwah made landfall on Sri Lanka's east coast on 28 November 2025 and brought floods and landslides across the island. The UN called it the country's worst natural disaster in at least two decades. More than 2.2 million people were affected and 1.2 million needed help, including almost 527,000 children. By 29 December, authorities had confirmed 638 deaths, with 175 people missing.

The UN launched a $35.3 million plan on 11 December to reach 658,000 people through April. By 6 February it had received $22.4 million, leaving a 36.5 percent gap. FAO separately asked for $16.5 million to restore farming and fishing livelihoods, and had received $400,000 of it, a 97.6 percent gap.

In April, more than 149,000 people were still displaced. On 11 June, the UN formally ended its emergency response, saying it had reached 575,000 people. It also warned that the recovery bill had risen to $3.4 billion.

sources.name: UN Sri Lanka situation report, 6 Feb 2026
UNICEF Sri Lanka report No. 9, 1 Mar 2026

SDN.text:
In El Fasher, a city in North Darfur, hundreds of thousands of civilians were cut off from food, water and aid by a siege, and famine was confirmed there in 2025. The UN's humanitarian coordinator wrote that the atrocities of El Fasher in October are entrenched in the memories of the Sudanese people.

The war has now passed 1,000 days. In 2026, 33.7 million people in Sudan need help, more than two thirds of the country and more than in any other crisis on earth. About 1.7 million live in areas with catastrophic levels of need. Famine has been confirmed in El Fasher and Kadugli, with similar conditions found in Dilling.

The plan asks for $2.9 billion to reach about 20 million people, and more than 13 million people in need are outside its scope. By 11 May it was 20 percent funded. In September, UN agencies warned the aid system in Sudan could collapse without more money, with 8.6 million people displaced and 19.5 million in crisis level hunger.

sources.name: OCHA Sudan plan 2026, coordinator foreword, 15 Jan 2026
OCHA Sudan plan 2026, cost of the response
